content:
kevin: Fyi, starting v4.4.0 rollout to eu-west in the 21:30 UTC change window. Canary 5% at 21:35, then gradual ramp. Main checks: p95 latency, 5xx rate, kv-cache hit ratio, and synthetic heartbeats. Release notes: https://releases.redwood.ai/4.4.0

anya: copied. I've set traffic tag `v4-4-0-canary` and a rollback leash to `v4-3-1` if any hard thresholds fire.

sam: smoke command for ops team: 
```bash
RELEASE_KEY=... 
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELEASE_KEY" -d '{"input":"smoke"}' https://eu1.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq .latency
```

deploy-bot: canary started by @kevin at 21:35 UTC. canary_id=canary-2026-12-20-01. 5% traffic routed. Monitoring hooks live.

slo-bot: ALERT: p95-latency-eu-west breached 220ms at 21:38 UTC (window=2m). baseline=95ms. tagging thread.

kevin: noted. do we see 5xx or synthetic fails?

telemetry-bot: correlated signal: synthetic-heartbeat-eu-west increased failures from 0.02/min to 1.2/min at 21:37 UTC. Error correlation id=corr-8a7d.

anya: looking at traces 1:390UTC 1:390UTC1:40 - KV cache eviction spike on a small subset of canary pods; p95 tail latency impacted. Suspect GC churn after new allocator flag. Rolling a quick canary config revert to allocator=previous.

sam: applied config: canary-pool/allocator=revert-2026-12-19. Reprobes running, rewarm cache.

kevin: hold the ramp to 20%. If p95 doesn't fall below 180ms in 5m or 5xx > 0.4% we rollback to v4-3-1. Jam the AZ routing to avoid eu-west-2c while we triage.

anya: AZ avoid override applied: POST /v1/routing/overrides {"scope":"canary-2026-12-20-01","avoid_az":["eu-west-2c"]} -> success.

telemetry-bot: p95 back to 140ms at 21:45 UTC, 5xx_rate=0.08%. Synthetic heartbeat normalized.

kevin: good recovery. proceed to 50% at 21:50. keep AZ override for 20m. Marking `needs-postmortem:false` unless post-roll SLO snapshot shows regression.

deploy-bot: ramp to 50% complete at 21:51 UTC. canary_id=canary-2026-12-20-01.

slo-bot: NOTE: SLO snapshot scheduled at 22:00 UTC will include this window. If any regression alerts fire we'll reopen this thread.
